posts.headline: Seattle · 星期六亲子精选
highlights: 🎨 可以体验艺术与文化主题活动。💛 适合安排周末亲子时光。
posts.description: Get up close with Ai Weiwei’s Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010) at the Olympic Sculpture Park, where you can walk among these monumental sculptures. Consisting of 12 zodiac head sculptures arranged in an arcing semicircle, each animal in Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads stands over ten feet tall and weighs over 1500 pounds. The sculptures are installed in order of the traditional Chinese zodiac cycle: Rat, Ox, Tiger, Rabbit, Dragon, Snake, Horse, Ram, Monkey, Rooster, Dog, and Boar. The works reconceive 12 zodiac heads that once decorated an 18th-century Qing imperial fountain before they were looted during the Second Opium War (1856–1860). Seven are based on the original heads that have survived, and Ai researched and reimagined the five animals still missing to complete the zodiac. This work embodies Ai’s long engagement with questioning the tendency to value the real over the fake and the original over the copy. Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads joins over twenty monumental sculptures in the park, including The Eagle (1971) by Alexander Calder, Wake (2002–3) by Richard Serra, and Seattle Cloud Cover (2006) by Teresita Fernández. See this temporary installation situated in the Ackerly Meadow, just outside of the PACCAR Pavilion at the Olympic Sculpture Park. posts.title: Downtown Issaquah Story Stroll: ‘Watercress’
posts.headline: Bellevue · 星期日亲子精选
highlights: 📚 可以体验教育与探索主题活动。💛 适合安排周末亲子时光。
posts.description: The Downtown Issaquah Association celebrates its latest Story Stroll™ “edutainment” program along with the Issaquah Library with the fanciful, heartwarming book “Watercress” written by Andrea Wange and illustrated by Jason Chin. The Story Stroll™ features a story about the power of sharing memories—including the painful ones—and the way our heritage stays with and shapes us, even when we don’t see it. Author Andrea Wang calls this moving, autobiographical story “both an apology and a love letter to my parents.” It’s a bittersweet, delicate look at how sharing the difficult parts of our histories can create powerful new moments of family history and help connect us to our roots.

posts.description: The Olympia Harbor Days Festival, a free event offered every Labor Day weekend, is an award-winning free and family-friendly event that showcases many of the vintage tugboats of the Puget Sound with a walk-aboard show at the docks and races in the bay. Visitors to the event may also find tall ships, steamships, other historic vessels of 20th-century commerce, tribal canoes and current recreational small watercraft. Harbor cruises on Budd Bay are also offered. On land, festival attendees enjoy great food, great music, great artisans, plus nautical and marine-themed attractions, and hands-on activities, including Olympia’s tugboat heritage, tribal history and the working waterfront with Port of Olympia tours. All in all, there are more than 300 things to do and see. Bring your kids to this family-friendly maritime celebration and fuel their dreams of working on the water and sailing the world when they grow up. Olympia Harbor Days Festival also includes locally hand-built small watercraft, tribal cultural sharings, sand carving, a Lego Harbor Build, and dancing pirates, just to name a few. posts.description: The Lake Wilderness Arboretum and Maple Valley Library have partnered together to bring a StoryWalk to Maple Valley. StoryWalk is an innovative approach to encouraging people of all ages to get out and walk while enjoying wonderful children’s books. With her wealth of experience, Sharon Chastain, the children’s librarian at the Maple Valley Library, selects the best children’s books for this story walk project. Then the pages are installed in frames along the Arboretum’s Main Looping Trail so as September StoryWalk: This month’s StoryWalk selection, The Girl with Big, Big Questions written by Britney Winn Lee, is a lively picture book about a persistent girl and her quest for knowledge. It celebrates the spirit of curiousity and shows us that asking questions is how we learn and grow – perhaps the perfect book to read as a new school year starts. So get outside, go for a walk, and read a book.

posts.description: Sky Valley Heritage Hunt Adventure is closer than you think. Celebrate America’s 250th Anniversary by exploring the history, scenery, and small-town charm of the Sky Valley through this free, self-guided Heritage Hunt. Travel through seven participating Highway 2 communities: Monroe Sultan Startup Gold Bar Index Grotto Skykomish At each stop, you’ll discover historic landmarks, local stories, public art, scenic locations, and hidden gems that many travelers drive past every day. Using your phone, you’ll scan QR codes at official Heritage Hunt stops to check in, learn about each location, answer a short trivia question, and track your progress as you explore. Whether you’re planning a family outing, a weekend road trip, or simply looking for a new reason to explore the Highway 2 corridor, the Heritage Hunt is designed to help you experience Sky Valley in a whole new way. Registration is free and includes: Free team registration A self-guided adventure you can complete at your own pace Interactive historical stops across seven communities Trivia, photo opportunities, and local discoveries Progress tracking throughout your journey Eligibility to earn a commemorative America 250 Challenge Coin upon successful completion, while supplies last The Sky Valley Heritage Hunt is appropriate for families, couples, friends, history enthusiasts, photographers, and anyone who enjoys scenic dr
